* fix(ci): detect union-duplicated entry text in brain log/ledger

UNION-MERGE-DUPLICATES-EDITED-LOG-AND-LEDGER-ENTRIES-SILENTLY-01.
When one side edits the last entry of sahool-brain/log.md or
decisions/ledger.md and the other appends, merge=union keeps the edited
lines next to their originals with git rc=0, and the existing identity
nets (gap-ID headings, registry rows) cannot see it: log/ledger headings
are dates, not IDs.

Measured in a temp repo: union duplicates the edited LINES (edited block
then original block), not the whole entry; the heading repeats only when
it is inside the edited block. So brain_duplicate_gap_identity_guard.py
gains a third net, scoped to log.md and ledger.md:
  1. identical substantive lines (>=30 chars, whitespace-normalized)
     within one entry;
  2. prefix-edit (one line is a prefix of the other) within one entry;
  3. SequenceMatcher ratio >= 0.9 only inside one contiguous block (no
     blank line between), which drops the only measured false positive
     (log.md:9131/9138 late-merge template, 0.932, separate paragraphs);
  4. an identical heading whose body is a >= 0.9 copy.
Same date under the same heading with different content passes.

Pre-existing duplicates on 5472740e (4 pairs: log.md 7875/7879 and
7876/7880; ledger.md 2102/2104 and 2103/2105) are frozen in
NEAR_DUPLICATE_BASELINE keyed by (path, line sha256[:16] x2) -> pair
count, so a third copy still fails. Stale entries are enforced by a
live-tree test, not inside check(), because preflight also runs the
guard on reduced fixture trees.

Wave 3: python-jose → PyJWT, gateway rate limit, frontend readyz, well-blend quality, two P0 guards (#1198)

* fix(irrigation): compute blend EC and ion-based SAR from mixing_ratio

WELL-BLEND-WATER-QUALITY-NOT-COMPUTED-01: the binding resolver returned
mixing_ratio verbatim and nothing computed the quality of the water
actually applied to a multi-source field.

- core.irrigation_water_analysis.compute_blend_water_quality:
  EC = sum(f_i * EC_i) (declared linear-mixing approximation);
  SAR = Na / sqrt((Ca+Mg)/2) on volume-weighted Na/Ca/Mg (meq/L), reusing
  compute_sar - never a weighted mean of per-source SARs. Missing/invalid
  ions or EC => not_computable with a named reason (value None, never 0).
  Ratios: sole source with NULL ratio = 1.0 (v214 contract); otherwise
  every ratio declared, finite, in [0,1], summing to 1 within 1e-3
  (normalised only inside that tolerance), else the blend is rejected.
- irrigation_source_binding.summarize_blend_water_quality adapts resolved
  bindings; live samples carry EC only (no ion columns), so live SAR is
  honestly not_computable (source_ions_missing).
- MPC recommendation reports blend_water_quality in the salinity
  provenance and in the blocked response; advisory only - the
  worst-source gate is unchanged (tested).

Witness: tests/test_irrigation_blend_water_quality.py (21) and
tests_v9 test_route_recommendation_reports_blend_water_quality /
test_route_blend_quality_does_not_relax_the_worst_source_gate - RED on
origin/main (ImportError / KeyError), GREEN here.

* fix(frontend): rate-limit the Railway public gateway proxy routes

RAILWAY-GATEWAY-HAS-NO-RATE-LIMIT-01: frontend/nginx.conf (rendered by
deploy/railway/render_frontend.py and served as the public Railway
gateway) had zero limit_req while nginx.v9.conf has 32.

- limit_req_zone x3 keyed on the client address: last X-Forwarded-For
  hop (appended by the nearest proxy, not client-writable), falling back
  to $remote_addr. $remote_addr alone is Railway's edge proxy, i.e. one
  shared bucket for every user. real_ip deliberately not used: it would
  change X-Real-IP/X-Forwarded-For forwarded to backends.
- limit_req with burst + nodelay on every proxy location: /api/* and
  /tts/ 20r/s burst 40; /api/raster/ tiles 50r/s burst 200; /auth/ 5r/s
  burst 20. limit_req_status 429 at server level.
- Not limited: /healthz, /readyz, /runtime-identity, exact health
  probes, static assets, SPA shell, /ws/. No server-level limit_req.
- Loopback peers exempt (container probe; the CI runtime suite runs
  with --network=host). Loopback only: a private-range exemption could
  cover the Railway edge and disable the limit.

Witness tests_v9/test_frontend_gateway_rate_limit_contract.py (unit,
9) checks the source and the Railway-rendered config: 4 red on the
origin/main config, 9 green after.

* security(jwt): route 11 consumer decodes through shared decoder in observe mode

JWT-DECODE-OUTSIDE-SHARED-SECURITY-01 (partial). Adds
shared/security/access_tokens.decode_access_token(token, key, *, algorithm,
backend, site): the caller's own library (pyjwt|jose), key and one pinned
algorithm (RS256|HS256) with aud=sahool, so each decode verdict and its
native exception type are unchanged. The stricter claim policy
(exp/sub/aud/iss present, issuer allow-listed) is evaluated in observe mode
by default (owner decision 2026-10-01, #1118): would-be rejections are
counted per (site, reason), exported as
sahool_access_token_claim_policy_would_reject_total when prometheus_client is
present, and logged without the token or any claim value.
SAHOOL_ACCESS_TOKEN_CLAIM_POLICY=enforce turns the verdict into a rejection.

An empty verification key is rejected regardless of mode: python-jose 3.5.0
accepts a token HMAC-signed with an empty key, so video-processor without
JWT_SECRET accepted forged identities for any tenant (now 401).

Migrated (11 calls, 8 files): guardrails-engine x2, local-ai-rag, odoo-bridge,
sahool-platform main/routers.auth/chat_proxy_reference (2 -> 1),
supervisor-agent, vegetation runtime, video-processor.
Remaining, declared in the ratchet and the witness allowlist:
actuator_runtime.py (GATE-01 frozen), services/auth x3 (issuer, moves last),
mcp market_server + oauth_middleware (dev-tree shared package shadow pinned by
test_season_api_static), tts-service (deferred to avoid overlap with the
readiness slice; decision-service has no direct decode call).
python-jose import in shared/security/access_tokens.py is now lazy so
PyJWT-only images can import the module.

Witness: tests_v9/test_jwt_decode_shared_decoder.py (red on origin/main:
11 failed + 30 errors; green: 42 passed).

* fix(frontend): /readyz reports the frontend gateway's own readiness

FRONTEND-READYZ-IMPERSONATES-PLATFORM-READINESS-01. The frontend gateway
(frontend/nginx.conf, rendered as the public Railway gateway) proxied
/readyz to the platform's /readyz, so it reported platform readiness
under the frontend's name; gating a frontend deploy on it would freeze
whenever the platform is down.

/readyz is now answered by nginx itself, with no backend:
200 {"status":"ready","component":"frontend-gateway"} when the config
loaded (valid config, resolver present for the `resolve` upstreams) and
the SPA shell is servable, else 503 {"status":"not_ready",...}. It stays
exempt from limit_req. /runtime-identity is still proxied. No caller of
the frontend /readyz needed platform readiness (observability smoke and
ops scripts target the v9 gateway or the platform directly), so no
alias path was added. Railway's frontend healthcheck stays on /healthz.

Witness: tests_v9/test_gateway_operational_endpoints_contract.py checks
the source and Railway-rendered config (red on origin/main, green here)
plus a falsification case; frontend/tests/test_nginx_runtime.py now
asserts /readyz is 200 with no backend, 503 without the SPA shell, and
never reaches the platform. Contract doc updated.

* fix(ci): detect union-duplicated entry text in brain log/ledger

UNION-MERGE-DUPLICATES-EDITED-LOG-AND-LEDGER-ENTRIES-SILENTLY-01.
When one side edits the last entry of sahool-brain/log.md or
decisions/ledger.md and the other appends, merge=union keeps the edited
lines next to their originals with git rc=0, and the existing identity
nets (gap-ID headings, registry rows) cannot see it: log/ledger headings
are dates, not IDs.

Measured in a temp repo: union duplicates the edited LINES (edited block
then original block), not the whole entry; the heading repeats only when
it is inside the edited block. So brain_duplicate_gap_identity_guard.py
gains a third net, scoped to log.md and ledger.md:
  1. identical substantive lines (>=30 chars, whitespace-normalized)
     within one entry;
  2. prefix-edit (one line is a prefix of the other) within one entry;
  3. SequenceMatcher ratio >= 0.9 only inside one contiguous block (no
     blank line between), which drops the only measured false positive
     (log.md:9131/9138 late-merge template, 0.932, separate paragraphs);
  4. an identical heading whose body is a >= 0.9 copy.
Same date under the same heading with different content passes.

Pre-existing duplicates on 5472740e (4 pairs: log.md 7875/7879 and
7876/7880; ledger.md 2102/2104 and 2103/2105) are frozen in
NEAR_DUPLICATE_BASELINE keyed by (path, line sha256[:16] x2) -> pair
count, so a third copy still fails. Stale entries are enforced by a
live-tree test, not inside check(), because preflight also runs the
guard on reduced fixture trees.

Two new mutations registered (detection disabled, block constraint
lifted); both are killed by their named tests. GUARD_CATALOGUE.md needs
regeneration for the mutation count (432 -> 434).

* fix(ci): fake-connection debt ratchet counts a class, not a naming convention

FAKE-CONNECTION-RATCHET-COUNTS-A-NAMING-CONVENTION-NOT-A-CLASS-01.

The ratchet matched `class _?Fake…(Conn|Pool)` / `fake_conn…` / `fake_pool…`
as text, so stand-ins named `_Conn`, `Connection`, `_Pool` or
`fake_tenant_connection` were invisible while claiming DB behaviour
(tenant predicate, JSONB-as-text). Detection is now structural (AST):
connection-shaped classes anchored on the asyncpg signature, pool-shaped
classes (not locks, not adapters around a real driver), patches of a DB
connection supplier whose replacement never reaches asyncpg, and
configured mocks/stubs. Proxies around a live connection, HTTP/Redis/job
fakes and live-PG `_connect` patches are excluded and pinned by tests.

claiming DB-enforced semantics (outstanding 1 -> 12 after 8 live
settlements). No test file was renamed or edited.

(carried, never derived by --generate) must name every site with a

  rejection and the observe/enforce claim policy are unchanged.

- tts-service: import/call swap to decode_access_token (python-jose semantics).
- local-ai-rag, odoo-bridge, video-processor: backend="jose" ->
  claim_semantics="python-jose"; except JWTError -> PyJWTError.
- shared/fcm.py: RS256 assertion signed with PyJWT (header alg RS256/typ JWT).
- requirements: python-jose[cryptography] -> PyJWT[crypto]==2.15.0 in 9 files;
